title: Why is My Render Black
summary: Official Derivative troubleshooting checklist for black or empty Render TOP output, covering checkerboard viewer diagnosis, lighting/material fixes, camera clipping/FOV, Geometry parameter patterns, COMP and SOP render flags, SOP bounds/alpha/normals inspection, light display flags, Base COMP nesting, and fallback default render setups.
key_concepts: light in front of the geometry
guidance: Use this article as the first troubleshooting path for black, transparent, or empty Render TOP output.
Switch the TOP viewer background to checkerboard: all checkerboard means nothing is rendering, while black means something is present but likely not lit.
Check lighting and material response before changing graph structure; add a light, put it in front of geometry, or use emit/ambient color or a white Constant MAT.
If geometry may be outside the camera, test Render TOP Cube Map mode and verify Camera COMP Near and Far clipping planes.
Set the Render TOP Geometry parameter to a broad pattern such as * while debugging, then confirm Geometry COMP Render flag, Geometry COMP Render parameter, and SOP Render flags.
Inspect SOP bounds, point/vertex alpha, and normals; attach SOP to DAT when numeric attributes need inspection.
For lights to affect geometry, the light display flag must be on, and lights/cameras should not be nested in Base COMPs that exclude them from the Geometry Viewer.
When still stuck, try a default Camera COMP, Geometry COMP, Light COMP, and new Render TOP before chasing rarer causes such as back-face culling or blend modes.
